claim: In the mammalian neocortex, inhibition is important for dynamically balancing excitation and shaping the response properties of cells and circuits.
source: In the mammalian neocortex, inhibition is important for dynamically balancing excitation and shaping the response properties of cells and circuits.
evidence: This is a general statement about cortical function supported by established scientific knowledge in neuroscience.

claim: The various computational functions of inhibition are thought to be mediated by different inhibitory neuron types.
source: The various computational functions of inhibition are thought to be mediated by different inhibitory neuron types, of which a large diversity exists in several species.
evidence: This represents a theoretical framework in neuroscience based on accumulated research.

claim: A large diversity of inhibitory neuron types exists in several species.
source: The various computational functions of inhibition are thought to be mediated by different inhibitory neuron types, of which a large diversity exists in several species.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge about inhibitory neuron diversity.

claim: Current understanding of the function and connectivity of distinct inhibitory neuron types has mainly derived from studies in transgenic mice.
source: Current understanding of the function and connectivity of distinct inhibitory neuron types has mainly derived from studies in transgenic mice.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field, representing established knowledge about research approaches.

claim: It is unknown whether knowledge gained from mouse studies applies to the non-human primate.
source: However, it is unknown whether knowledge gained from mouse studies applies to the non-human primate, the model system closest to humans.
evidence: This represents a knowledge gap in the field, inferred from the lack of comparative studies.

claim: The non-human primate is the model system closest to humans.
source: However, it is unknown whether knowledge gained from mouse studies applies to the non-human primate, the model system closest to humans.
evidence: This is based on established evolutionary and comparative biology knowledge.

claim: The lack of viral tools to selectively access inhibitory neuron types has been a major impediment to studying their function in the primate.
source: The lack of viral tools to selectively access inhibitory neuron types has been a major impediment to studying their function in the primate.
evidence: This is an inference about the state of the field and technical limitations.

claim: AAV-h56D induces transgene expression in GABAergic cells with up to 91–94% specificity in marmoset V1.
source: We show that in marmoset V1, AAV-h56D induces transgene expression in GABAergic cells with up to 91–94% specificity and 79% efficiency, but this depends on viral serotype and cortical layer.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript (Figure 4B).

claim: AAV-h56D induces transgene expression in GABAergic cells with 79% efficiency in marmoset V1.
source: We show that in marmoset V1, AAV-h56D induces transgene expression in GABAergic cells with up to 91–94% specificity and 79% efficiency, but this depends on viral serotype and cortical layer.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript (Figure 4C).

claim: The specificity and efficiency of AAV-h56D-mediated transgene expression depends on viral serotype and cortical layer.
source: We show that in marmoset V1, AAV-h56D induces transgene expression in GABAergic cells with up to 91–94% specificity and 79% efficiency, but this depends on viral serotype and cortical layer.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing variation across serotypes and layers (Figure 4).

claim: AAV-PHP.eB-S5E2 induces transgene expression in PV cells across all cortical layers with up to 98% specificity in marmoset V1.
source: AAV-PHP.eB-S5E2 induces transgene expression in PV cells across all cortical layers with up to 98% specificity and 86–90% efficiency, depending on layer.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript (Figure 6B).

claim: AAV-PHP.eB-S5E2 induces transgene expression in PV cells with 86–90% efficiency, depending on layer.
source: AAV-PHP.eB-S5E2 induces transgene expression in PV cells across all cortical layers with up to 98% specificity and 86–90% efficiency, depending on layer.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript (Figure 6C).

claim: These viral vectors are promising tools for studying GABA and PV cell function and connectivity in the primate cortex.
source: Thus, these viral vectors are promising tools for studying GABA and PV cell function and connectivity in the primate cortex.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the experimental data on specificity and efficiency.

claim: Inhibitory neurons represent only 15–30% of all cortical neurons.
source: Although representing only 15–30% of all cortical neurons, inhibitory neurons profoundly influence cortical computations and cortical dynamics.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from previous studies in neuroscience.

claim: Inhibitory neurons profoundly influence cortical computations and cortical dynamics.
source: Although representing only 15–30% of all cortical neurons, inhibitory neurons profoundly influence cortical computations and cortical dynamics.
evidence: This is supported by established scientific knowledge in neuroscience.

claim: Inhibitory neurons influence how excitatory neurons integrate information.
source: For example, they influence how excitatory neurons integrate information, shape neuronal tuning properties, modulate neuronal responses based on sensory context and behavioral state, and maintain an appropriate dynamic range of cortical excitation (Ferster and Miller, 2000; Shapley et al., 2003; Tremblay et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Inhibitory neurons shape neuronal tuning properties.
source: For example, they influence how excitatory neurons integrate information, shape neuronal tuning properties, modulate neuronal responses based on sensory context and behavioral state, and maintain an appropriate dynamic range of cortical excitation (Ferster and Miller, 2000; Shapley et al., 2003; Tremblay et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Inhibitory neurons modulate neuronal responses based on sensory context and behavioral state.
source: For example, they influence how excitatory neurons integrate information, shape neuronal tuning properties, modulate neuronal responses based on sensory context and behavioral state, and maintain an appropriate dynamic range of cortical excitation (Ferster and Miller, 2000; Shapley et al., 2003; Tremblay et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Inhibitory neurons maintain an appropriate dynamic range of cortical excitation.
source: For example, they influence how excitatory neurons integrate information, shape neuronal tuning properties, modulate neuronal responses based on sensory context and behavioral state, and maintain an appropriate dynamic range of cortical excitation (Ferster and Miller, 2000; Shapley et al., 2003; Tremblay et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A large diversity of inhibitory neuron types has been identified in several species, each having distinct chemical, electrophysiological, and morphological properties.
source: These various functions of inhibition are thought to be mediated by different inhibitory neuron types, of which a large diversity has been identified in several species, each having distinct chemical, electrophysiological, and morphological properties (Ascoli et al., 2008; Burkhalter, 2008; Kubota et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In mouse cortex, the expression of specific molecular markers identifies three major, largely non-overlapping classes of inhibitory neurons: parvalbumin- (PV), somatostatin- (SOM), and serotonin receptor (5HT3aR)-expressing neurons.
source: In mouse cortex, the expression of specific molecular markers identifies three major, largely non-overlapping classes of inhibitory neurons: parvalbumin- (PV), somatostatin- (SOM), and serotonin receptor (5HT3aR, a larger class which includes vasoactive intestinal peptide or VIP cells)-expressing neurons (Xu et al., 2010; Rudy et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The 5HT3aR class is a larger class which includes vasoactive intestinal peptide or VIP cells.
source: In mouse cortex, the expression of specific molecular markers identifies three major, largely non-overlapping classes of inhibitory neurons: parvalbumin- (PV), somatostatin- (SOM), and serotonin receptor (5HT3aR, a larger class which includes vasoactive intestinal peptide or VIP cells)-expressing neurons (Xu et al., 2010; Rudy et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The creation of mouse lines selectively expressing Cre-recombinase in specific inhibitory neuron classes has led to a multitude of studies on the connectivity and function of each class.
source: The creation of mouse lines selectively expressing Cre-recombinase in specific inhibitory neuron classes has led to a multitude of studies on the connectivity and function of each class (Tremblay et al., 2016; Wood et al., 2017; Shin and Adesnik, 2023).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Distinct patterns of connectivity and function specific to each inhibitory neuron class are emerging from mouse studies.
source: Distinct patterns of connectivity and function specific to each inhibitory neuron class are emerging from these mouse studies, but it remains unknown whether insights gained from mouse apply to inhibitory neurons in higher species such as primates.
evidence: This is an inference based on the body of mouse research cited.

claim: It remains unknown whether insights gained from mouse apply to inhibitory neurons in higher species such as primates.
source: Distinct patterns of connectivity and function specific to each inhibitory neuron class are emerging from these mouse studies, but it remains unknown whether insights gained from mouse apply to inhibitory neurons in higher species such as primates.
evidence: This represents a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Understanding cortical inhibitory neuron function in the primate is critical for understanding cortical function and dysfunction in the model system closest to humans.
source: Understanding cortical inhibitory neuron function in the primate is critical for understanding cortical function and dysfunction in the model system closest to humans, where cortical inhibitory neuron dysfunction has been implicated in many neurological and psychiatric disorders, such as epilepsy, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer's disease (Cheah et al., 2012; Verret et al., 2012; Mukherjee et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an inference about the importance of primate research based on evolutionary proximity to humans.

claim: Cortical inhibitory neuron dysfunction has been implicated in many neurological and psychiatric disorders, such as epilepsy, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer's disease.
source: Understanding cortical inhibitory neuron function in the primate is critical for understanding cortical function and dysfunction in the model system closest to humans, where cortical inhibitory neuron dysfunction has been implicated in many neurological and psychiatric disorders, such as epilepsy, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer's disease (Cheah et al., 2012; Verret et al., 2012; Mukherjee et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Two recent studies have developed specific promoters or enhancers that restrict transgene expression from recombinant adeno-associated viral vectors (AAV) to GABAergic neurons, specifically the mDlx enhancer and the h56D promoter, in both rodents and primates.
source: In particular, two recent studies have developed specific promoters or enhancers that restrict transgene expression from recombinant adeno-associated viral vectors (AAV) to GABAergic neurons, specifically the mDlx enhancer (Dimidschstein et al., 2016) and the h56D promoter (Mehta et al., 2019), in both rodents and primates.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Viral strategies to restrict gene expression to PV neurons have been recently developed.
source: Viral strategies to restrict gene expression to PV neurons have also been recently developed (Mehta et al., 2019; Vormstein-Schneider et al., 2020; Mich et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The study tested three serotypes of the h56D promoter-AAV that restricts gene expression to GABAergic neurons.
source: Here, we report results from the two vector types that have shown the greatest specificity of transgene expression in marmoset primary visual cortex (V1); specifically, we have tested three serotypes of the h56D promoter-AAV that restricts gene expression to GABAergic neurons (Mehta et al., 2019), and one serotype of the S5E2 enhancer-AAV that restricts gene expression to PV cells (Vormstein-Schneider et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: The study tested one serotype of the S5E2 enhancer-AAV that restricts gene expression to PV cells.
source: Here, we report results from the two vector types that have shown the greatest specificity of transgene expression in marmoset primary visual cortex (V1); specifically, we have tested three serotypes of the h56D promoter-AAV that restricts gene expression to GABAergic neurons (Mehta et al., 2019), and one serotype of the S5E2 enhancer-AAV that restricts gene expression to PV cells (Vormstein-Schneider et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: The laminar distribution of reporter protein expression mediated by the GABA- and PV-enhancer AAVs resembles the laminar distribution of GABA-immunoreactive (GABA+) and PV-immunoreactive (PV+) cells, respectively, in marmoset V1.
source: Using injections of these viral vectors in marmoset V1, combined with immunohistochemical identification of GABA and PV neurons, we find that the laminar distribution of reporter protein expression mediated by the GABA- and PV-enhancer AAVs validated in this study resembles the laminar distribution of GABA-immunoreactive (GABA+) and PV-immunoreactive (PV+) cells, respectively, in marmoset V1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing viral expression to immunohistochemistry (Figures 4A and 6A).

claim: Reporter protein expression mediated by the h56D-AAV is specific and robust.
source: Reporter protein expression mediated by the h56D-AAV is specific and robust, but the degree of specificity and coverage depended on serotype and cortical layer.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4.

claim: The degree of specificity and coverage of h56D-AAV-mediated reporter protein expression depended on serotype and cortical layer.
source: Reporter protein expression mediated by the h56D-AAV is specific and robust, but the degree of specificity and coverage depended on serotype and cortical layer.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4.

claim: About 92% of PV cells in marmoset V1 are GABA+.
source: We found that about 92% of PV cells in marmoset V1 are GABA+, and reporter protein expression mediated by the S5E2-AAV shows up to 98% specificity and 86–90% coverage, depending on layer.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from double-labeling experiments (Figure 2E).

claim: Reporter protein expression mediated by the S5E2-AAV shows up to 98% specificity, depending on layer.
source: We found that about 92% of PV cells in marmoset V1 are GABA+, and reporter protein expression mediated by the S5E2-AAV shows up to 98% specificity and 86–90% coverage, depending on layer.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 6B.

claim: Reporter protein expression mediated by the S5E2-AAV shows 86–90% coverage, depending on layer.
source: We found that about 92% of PV cells in marmoset V1 are GABA+, and reporter protein expression mediated by the S5E2-AAV shows up to 98% specificity and 86–90% coverage, depending on layer.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 6C.

claim: The study validated three serotypes (1,7,9) of a pAAV-h56D-tdTomato and the AAV-PHP.eB-S5E2.tdTomato.
source: We validated three serotypes (1,7,9) of a pAAV-h56D-tdTomato (Mehta et al., 2019) and the AAV-PHP.eB-S5E2.tdTomato (Vormstein-Schneider et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: The study reports results from 10 viral injections, of which 3 injections of AAV-h56D-tdTomato, and 7 injections of AAV-PHP.eB-S5E2.tdTomato, made in 4 marmoset monkeys.
source: We report results from 10 viral injections, of which 3 injections of AAV-h56D-tdTomato, and 7 injections of AAV-PHP.eB-S5E2.tdTomato, made in 4 marmoset monkeys (see 'Materials and methods' and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the study.

claim: Tissue sections through V1 were double immunoreacted for GABA and PV and imaged on a fluorescent microscope.
source: Tissue sections through V1 were double immunoreacted for GABA and PV and imaged on a fluorescent microscope.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: The laminar distribution of viral-induced tdTomato (tdT) expression as well as of GABA+ and PV+ cells revealed by immunohistochemistry was quantified.
source: We quantified the laminar distribution of viral-induced tdTomato (tdT) expression as well as of GABA+ and PV+ cells revealed by immunohistochemistry (IHC), and counted double- and triple-labeled cells to determine the specificity and coverage of viral-induced tdT expression across marmoset V1 layers (see 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Double- and triple-labeled cells were counted to determine the specificity and coverage of viral-induced tdT expression across marmoset V1 layers.
source: We quantified the laminar distribution of viral-induced tdTomato (tdT) expression as well as of GABA+ and PV+ cells revealed by immunohistochemistry (IHC), and counted double- and triple-labeled cells to determine the specificity and coverage of viral-induced tdT expression across marmoset V1 layers (see 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: GABA+ and PV+ cells were counted within 2 × 100-µm-wide regions of interest (ROIs) spanning all layers in dorsal V1 anterior to the posterior pole, for a total of six ROIs in three tissue sections selected randomly.
source: To this goal, in each section used for analysis, we counted GABA+ and PV+ cells within 2 × 100-µm-wide regions of interest (ROIs) spanning all layers in dorsal V1 anterior to the posterior pole, for a total of six ROIs in three tissue sections selected randomly.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Cortical layer boundaries were determined using DAPI and/or PV staining.
source: Cortical layer boundaries were determined using DAPI and/or PV staining (Figure 1B and C), as we found that PV-IHC reveals laminar boundaries consistent with those defined by DAPI.
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: PV-IHC reveals laminar boundaries consistent with those defined by DAPI.
source: Cortical layer boundaries were determined using DAPI and/or PV staining (Figure 1B and C), as we found that PV-IHC reveals laminar boundaries consistent with those defined by DAPI.
evidence: This is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 1.

claim: Both GABA+ and PV+ cell percent and density peaked in layers (L) 2/3 and 4C.
source: Both GABA+ and PV+ cell percent and density peaked in layers (L) 2/3 and 4C.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and 2B.

claim: There was no significant difference in the percent of GABA+ cells in L2/3 (33% ± 2) vs. L4C (33.4% ± 3.1).
source: There was no significant difference in the percent or density of GABA+ cells in L2/3 (33% ± 2, and 1294 cells/mm2 ± 74.4, respectively) vs. L4C (33.4% ± 3.1, and 1052 cells/mm2 ± 42.2, respectively), as determined by a Bonferroni-corrected Kruskal–Wallis test (p=1.00, n = 6 ROIs across three sections, L2/3 vs. L4C in Figure 2A) or by a Bonferroni-corrected ANOVA (p=1.00, n = 6 ROIs across three sections, L2/3 vs. L4C in Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: There was no significant difference in the density of GABA+ cells in L2/3 (1294 cells/mm2 ± 74.4) vs. L4C (1052 cells/mm2 ± 42.2).
source: There was no significant difference in the percent or density of GABA+ cells in L2/3 (33% ± 2, and 1294 cells/mm2 ± 74.4, respectively) vs. L4C (33.4% ± 3.1, and 1052 cells/mm2 ± 42.2, respectively), as determined by a Bonferroni-corrected Kruskal–Wallis test (p=1.00, n = 6 ROIs across three sections, L2/3 vs. L4C in Figure 2A) or by a Bonferroni-corrected ANOVA (p=1.00, n = 6 ROIs across three sections, L2/3 vs. L4C in Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The percent of PV+ cells in L4C (42.3% ± 3.6) was not significantly different from that in L2/3 (31.3% ± 2.5).
source: Similarly, the percent and density of PV+ cells in L4C (42.3% ± 3.6, and 888 cells/mm2 ± 38.8, respectively) were not significantly different from those in L2/3 (31.3% ± 2.5 and 812 cells/mm2 ± 65, respectively; p=1.00 for both comparisons, n = 6 ROIs).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The density of PV+ cells in L4C (888 cells/mm2 ± 38.8) was not significantly different from that in L2/3 (812 cells/mm2 ± 65).
source: Similarly, the percent and density of PV+ cells in L4C (42.3% ± 3.6, and 888 cells/mm2 ± 38.8, respectively) were not significantly different from those in L2/3 (31.3% ± 2.5 and 812 cells/mm2 ± 65, respectively; p=1.00 for both comparisons, n = 6 ROIs).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The density of PV+ cells in L4C was significantly higher than that in all remaining layers.
source: However, the density of PV+ cells in L4C was significantly higher than that in all remaining layers (p=0.028005 for 4C vs. 4A/B, and <0.001 for 4C vs. all other layers; ANOVA with Bonferroni correction; n = 6 ROIs), and L2/3 PV+ density was significantly higher than L1, 5 and 6 (p=5.93E–11 for L2/3 vs. L1 and p=0.00037 L2/3 vs. L6, p=0.002 for L2/3 vs. L5, n = 6 ROIs), but not L4A/B (although the percent of PV+ cells in L2/3 was significantly higher than that in L4A/B; p=0.029 Bonferroni-corrected Kruskal–Wallis test, n = 6 ROIs).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: L2/3 PV+ density was significantly higher than L1, 5 and 6.
source: However, the density of PV+ cells in L4C was significantly higher than that in all remaining layers (p=0.028005 for 4C vs. 4A/B, and <0.001 for 4C vs. all other layers; ANOVA with Bonferroni correction; n = 6 ROIs), and L2/3 PV+ density was significantly higher than L1, 5 and 6 (p=5.93E–11 for L2/3 vs. L1 and p=0.00037 L2/3 vs. L6, p=0.002 for L2/3 vs. L5, n = 6 ROIs), but not L4A/B (although the percent of PV+ cells in L2/3 was significantly higher than that in L4A/B; p=0.029 Bonferroni-corrected Kruskal–Wallis test, n = 6 ROIs).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: L2/3 PV+ density was not significantly different from L4A/B.
source: However, the density of PV+ cells in L4C was significantly higher than that in all remaining layers (p=0.028005 for 4C vs. 4A/B, and <0.001 for 4C vs. all other layers; ANOVA with Bonferroni correction; n = 6 ROIs), and L2/3 PV+ density was significantly higher than L1, 5 and 6 (p=5.93E–11 for L2/3 vs. L1 and p=0.00037 L2/3 vs. L6, p=0.002 for L2/3 vs. L5, n = 6 ROIs), but not L4A/B (although the percent of PV+ cells in L2/3 was significantly higher than that in L4A/B; p=0.029 Bonferroni-corrected Kruskal–Wallis test, n = 6 ROIs).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The percent of PV+ cells in L2/3 was significantly higher than that in L4A/B.
source: However, the density of PV+ cells in L4C was significantly higher than that in all remaining layers (p=0.028005 for 4C vs. 4A/B, and <0.001 for 4C vs. all other layers; ANOVA with Bonferroni correction; n = 6 ROIs), and L2/3 PV+ density was significantly higher than L1, 5 and 6 (p=5.93E–11 for L2/3 vs. L1 and p=0.00037 L2/3 vs. L6, p=0.002 for L2/3 vs. L5, n = 6 ROIs), but not L4A/B (although the percent of PV+ cells in L2/3 was significantly higher than that in L4A/B; p=0.029 Bonferroni-corrected Kruskal–Wallis test, n = 6 ROIs).

claim: GABA+ cell density in L2/3 was significantly higher than that in all other layers except L4C.
source: GABA+ cell density in L2/3 was significantly higher than that in all other layers except L4C (p=0.028 vs. L4A/B and p=0.013 vs. L6, p=0.007 vs. L1 and p=0.005 vs. L5).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: GABA density in L4C did not differ from any other layers.
source: GABA density in L4C did not differ from any other layers, but the percent of GABA+ cells in L4C was significantly higher than that in L1 (p=0.009) and 4A/B (p=0.000022).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The percent of GABA+ cells in L4C was significantly higher than that in L1 and 4A/B.
source: GABA density in L4C did not differ from any other layers, but the percent of GABA+ cells in L4C was significantly higher than that in L1 (p=0.009) and 4A/B (p=0.000022).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Within each layer, GABA+ cell density was significantly higher than PV+ cell density.
source: As expected, within each layer, GABA+ cell density was significantly higher than PV+ cell density (p<0.05, one-sided t-test for equality of means, n = 6 ROIs).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In marmoset V1, there is an overall higher density of PV+ cells than in mouse V1, with density peaking in L2/3 and 4C.
source: In marmoset V1, there is an overall higher density of PV+ cells than in mouse V1, with density peaking in L2/3 and 4C.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of experimental data with published mouse data (Figure 2C).

claim: PV+ cell density in mouse V1 peaks in L4 and 5, and density in L2/3 is lower than that in all other layers.
source: In contrast, PV+ cell density in mouse V1 peaks in L4 and 5, and density in L2/3 is lower than that in all other layers (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on published mouse data cited from Xu et al., 2010.

claim: GABA+ cell density in marmoset V1 peaks in L2/3 followed by 4C.
source: GABA+ cell density in marmoset V1 peaks in L2/3 followed by 4C, whereas it peaks in L4 and 5 with a smaller third peak in L2/3 in mouse V1 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: GABA+ cell density in mouse V1 peaks in L4 and 5 with a smaller third peak in L2/3.
source: GABA+ cell density in marmoset V1 peaks in L2/3 followed by 4C, whereas it peaks in L4 and 5 with a smaller third peak in L2/3 in mouse V1 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on published mouse data cited from Xu et al., 2010.

claim: 92.3% ± 1.9 of PV+ cells across all layers were GABA+.
source: Counts of cells double labeled for GABA+ and PV+ revealed that 92.3% ± 1.9 of PV+ cells across all layers were GABA+, and that PV+ cells represent on average 61.4% ± 2.7 of all GABA+ cells, ranging from 54.5% ± 3.7 in L6 to 78.5% ± 5.6 in L4C (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from double-labeling experiments shown in Figure 2E.

claim: PV+ cells represent on average 61.4% ± 2.7 of all GABA+ cells.
source: Counts of cells double labeled for GABA+ and PV+ revealed that 92.3% ± 1.9 of PV+ cells across all layers were GABA+, and that PV+ cells represent on average 61.4% ± 2.7 of all GABA+ cells, ranging from 54.5% ± 3.7 in L6 to 78.5% ± 5.6 in L4C (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from double-labeling experiments shown in Figure 2E.

claim: PV+ cells represent 54.5% ± 3.7 of all GABA+ cells in L6.
source: Counts of cells double labeled for GABA+ and PV+ revealed that 92.3% ± 1.9 of PV+ cells across all layers were GABA+, and that PV+ cells represent on average 61.4% ± 2.7 of all GABA+ cells, ranging from 54.5% ± 3.7 in L6 to 78.5% ± 5.6 in L4C (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from double-labeling experiments shown in Figure 2E.

claim: PV+ cells represent 78.5% ± 5.6 of all GABA+ cells in L4C.
source: Counts of cells double labeled for GABA+ and PV+ revealed that 92.3% ± 1.9 of PV+ cells across all layers were GABA+, and that PV+ cells represent on average 61.4% ± 2.7 of all GABA+ cells, ranging from 54.5% ± 3.7 in L6 to 78.5% ± 5.6 in L4C (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from double-labeling experiments shown in Figure 2E.

claim: In mouse V1, PV+ cells represent about 40% of all GABA cells.
source: This differs from mouse V1 in which PV+ cells represent about 40% of all GABA cells (Xu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on published mouse data cited from Xu et al., 2010.

claim: Identical injection volumes of each serotype, delivered at three different cortical depths, resulted in viral expression regions that differed in both size as well as laminar distribution.
source: Identical injection volumes of each serotype, delivered at three different cortical depths (see 'Materials and methods'), resulted in viral expression regions that differed in both size as well as laminar distribution, suggesting the different serotypes may have different capacity of infecting cortical neurons and layers.
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The different serotypes may have different capacity of infecting cortical neurons and layers.
source: Identical injection volumes of each serotype, delivered at three different cortical depths (see 'Materials and methods'), resulted in viral expression regions that differed in both size as well as laminar distribution, suggesting the different serotypes may have different capacity of infecting cortical neurons and layers.
evidence: This is an inference based on observed differences in viral expression patterns.

claim: The AAV7 injection resulted in the smallest expression region, which was biased to the superficial and deep layers, with only a few cells expressing tdT in the middle layers.
source: The AAV7 injection resulted in the smallest expression region, which additionally was biased to the superficial and deep layers, with only a few cells expressing tdT in the middle layers (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: AAV9 and AAV1 resulted in larger expression regions, which involved all cortical layers.
source: AAV9 (Figure 3A) and AAV1 (Figure 3C) resulted in larger expression regions, which involved all cortical layers.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3A and 3C.

claim: The differences in the size of the expression region are likely due to different tropism and/or viral spread of the different serotypes.
source: Given identical volumes and titers used for the AAV9 and AAV7 injections (injected volume of the AAV1 was the same but titer was higher; see Supplementary file 1), as well as identical post-injection survival times for all three serotypes, the differences in the size of the expression region are likely due to different tropism and/or viral spread of the different serotypes.
